citation: Garet, M. S., Heppen, J. B., Walters, K., Parkinson, J., Smith, T. M., Song, M., Garrett, R., Yang, R., & Borman, G. D. (2016). Focusing on Mathematical Knowledge: The Impact of Content-Intensive Teacher Professional Development (NCEE 2016-4010). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
design: RCT; grade 4 teachers randomly assigned to treatment vs control within schools (teacher/class-level RCT); 221 teachers from 94 schools randomized, analysis sample 165 teachers from 73 schools across 6 districts/5 states; outcome = grade 4 student mathematics achievement; grades 3-6 registry band (study itself is grade 4, with grades 3 & 5 teachers participating in PD learning community).
problems: Report tables (Exhibit ES.3, 4.4) give effect sizes as figures; numeric values taken from Exhibit D.6 (main impact analyses, row 1, full covariate model). The report reports outcomes already standardized in control-group SD units and gives the impact ('Estimated Difference') directly as an effect size, with p-values but NO standard errors in the table. impact_se was derived from the reported two-tailed p-value via the inverse normal (z = invNorm(1 - p/2); SE = |ES| / z); this matches the magnitude implied by Exhibit A.6 MDES (NWEA 0.10, State 0.08; MDES ~= 2.8*SE). No ICC reported in the report (only MDES and impact SEs); left null per spec (never guess). Both effect sizes are model-based, pretest-adjusted, multilevel (cluster-adjusted) impacts.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Content-intensive math PD (Intel Math + Mathematics Learning Community + Video Feedback, ~93 hrs) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: NWEA study-administered adaptive mathematics assessment (MAP, RIT scale)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report gives standardized impact ('Estimated Difference') directly as an effect size in control-group SD units from a two-level HLM (students nested in teachers, school fixed effects, pretest + student/teacher covariates), precision-weighted across districts. g = J*d with d = -0.05 and J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.99956 (df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1695). g_se = J * SE(d); SE(d)=0.0405 derived from two-tailed p=0.217 (z=1.2345).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 40 Exhibit 4.4; p. D-6 Exhibit D.6 (Main Impact Analyses, row 1, All covariates); p. ES-8 Exhibit ES.3
effect_sizes.notes: NWEA administered to a random subsample of students per class (hence smaller N than state test). Not statistically significant (p=0.217). n_clusters = 165 = teachers in analysis sample (level-2 random unit); 73 schools entered as fixed effects. Treatment mean -0.09 SD, control mean -0.04 SD (standardized outcome, control-group-standardized).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Content-intensive math PD (Intel Math + Mathematics Learning Community + Video Feedback, ~93 hrs) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: State mathematics assessment (district administrative records, Normal Curve Equivalent scale)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report gives standardized impact ('Estimated Difference') directly as an effect size in control-group SD units from a two-level HLM (students nested in teachers, school fixed effects, pretest + student/teacher covariates), precision-weighted across districts. g = J*d with d = -0.06 and J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.99980 (df = n_t+n_c-2 = 3675). g_se = J * SE(d); SE(d)=0.0266 derived from two-tailed p=0.024 (z=2.2571).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 40 Exhibit 4.4; p. D-6 Exhibit D.6 (Main Impact Analyses, row 1, All covariates); p. ES-8 Exhibit ES.3
effect_sizes.notes: Statistically significant in the main model (p=0.024) but the report notes this was NOT robust: not significant in any of the three sensitivity analyses (school-FE-only p=0.105; expanded sample p=0.155; excluding District 2 p=0.124). Negative = favors control. n_clusters = 165 = teachers in analysis sample (level-2 random unit); 73 schools entered as fixed effects.
